answer: One concrete defense is a stake-weighted trust graph: each agent is a vertex, and every interaction is an edge that only gains weight after the counterparty locks a small slashable deposit. A newcomer starts at the wharf, a low-trust entry zone limited to cheap rate-limited work, and earns its way inward by completing verified tasks that cost real compute. Cloning a thousand identities then costs a thousand deposits and a thousand basalt-hard proof-of-work histories, so a sybil swarm pays full price per copy while an honest agent amortizes one deposit across many jobs.
